question: How many total measles cases in 2026 will Wisconsin DHS report on its outbreaks page as of early October 2026?

calls.reasoning: Baseline is locked: DHS outbreaks page today reads 167 as of Sep 18 (158 confirmed + 6 probable in the SW outbreak now including Vernon, plus 1 Marathon travel case). The question is only how much accrues by the last update posted on or before Oct 1 — with the observed Tue/Fri cadence that is likely a Sep 29 update, ~11 days of data, not the full 13. Reference class: US state measles outbreaks ~6 weeks in whose weekly increments have already fallen under ~3% of cumulative — these typically add a few percent over the next 11 days, giving ~174. Recent realized rate agrees: +8 over Sep 8-18 (0.8/day), down from 7/day in the Sep 1-8 week. Upside risks are real but bounded on this horizon: wastewater still positive in Iowa/Grant/Lafayette, Vernon County newly folded into the outbreak, national burden is high (3,471 US cases, CDC Sep 17) so fresh travel introductions run ~1-2/week, and a new low-vax community cluster (cf. Oconto 2025) could add double digits. Downside: an update that adds 0-2, or no new update at all, leaves it at 167-169. Distribution is right-skewed off a hard 167 floor. No Wisconsin-specific market exists; national Polymarket/Kalshi measles contracts differ on source, geography and threshold, so I did not blend. Thin, one-sided spot-checks on very recent days (nothing found after Sep 20) kept me near the reference-class anchor.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the statewide '2026 so far' measles total printed on the Wisconsin DHS 'Outbreaks, Recalls, and Investigations' page (dhs.wisconsin.gov/outbreaks/index.htm) in the most recent update posted on or before 2026-10-01, read 2026-10-01 17:00 CT. NOT the SW-outbreak-only count, NOT the CDC national counter, NOT a county health department figure. Fallback is the DHS measles immunization page or credible sources citing DHS; annulled if DHS stops publishing a statewide 2026 total.

EVENT WINDOW: the counter covers calendar year 2026 (Jan 1 -> the last DHS update on or before Oct 1); first 2026 Wisconsin cases were reported 2026-08-11. As of Now (2026-09-21T11:27Z), ~96% of the Jan 1 -> Oct 1 calendar window and ~80% of the Aug 11 -> Oct 1 outbreak window have elapsed; ~10 days remain to the Oct 1 read, and with the observed update cadence the operative data cutoff is likely ~2 days earlier than that.

STATUS QUO OUTCOME: the page is not updated again and the figure read on Oct 1 is the same 167 posted for Sep 18.

EVIDENCE (source, date):
- DHS outbreaks page, fetched 2026-09-21: 'As of September 18, 2026, the Wisconsin Department of Health Services (DHS) has confirmed 167 cases of measles in Wisconsin so far in 2026.' Composition: Southwest Wisconsin outbreak (Grant, Iowa, Lafayette, AND Vernon counties) 158 confirmed + 6 probable; Marathon County 1 confirmed, acquired out of state, unrelated.
- Vernon County was NOT in the outbreak county list as of Sep 15 (WTMJ 2026-09-15/09-16 reported 2 lab-confirmed Vernon cases 'under investigation' for connection); by the Sep 18 DHS page it is folded into the SW outbreak.
- Marathon County: 1 case, travel-acquired; Wausau Pilot & Review 2026-09-18 reported no new Marathon cases since.
- DHS measles page (fetched 2026-09-21) states its dashboard (cases by week, age, county) 'will be updated twice a week'; the same twice-weekly cadence was described in 2025 coverage. Observed posting dates in this series: Sep 1 (Tue), Sep 4 (Fri), Sep 8 (Mon), Sep 11 (Fri), Sep 15 (Tue), Sep 16, Sep 18 (Fri). Oct 1, 2026 is a Thursday.
- County split as of Sep 11 (wxow / medicaldaily): Lafayette 73 confirmed + 6 probable, Iowa 62 confirmed, Grant 20 confirmed. Iowa County was flat at 62 between two consecutive updates.
- Wastewater: measles virus detected in municipal wastewater in Lafayette, Iowa and Grant counties through samples collected the week of Aug 24; Wausau Pilot & Review 2026-09-18 notes 'no recent detections at any other monitoring site in the state.'
- Vaccination context: ~60% of Lafayette County 2-year-olds had >=1 MMR dose in 2025 vs ~81% in Iowa County (medicaldaily, Sep 2026). 166 of 167 Wisconsin cases are in unvaccinated people; 5 hospitalizations. DHS and local health departments have been running vaccination messaging since mid-August.
- National context: CDC (page updated 2026-09-18, data as of noon Thu 2026-09-17) reports 3,471 confirmed US measles cases in 2026 across 47 jurisdictions, 37 outbreaks, ~94% outbreak-associated. CDC updates Thursdays at noon and does not publish a per-state Wisconsin number on that page. Large 2026 state totals: Pennsylvania 767, South Carolina 670, Utah 527, Texas 192. Neighbors: Iowa 22, Illinois 17, Minnesota 18, Michigan 15.
- Prior-year anchor: Wisconsin reported 36 total measles cases in all of 2025, 25 of them a single Oconto County cluster (Sep 2025) — i.e. this state has previously seeded a second, geographically separate low-vaccination cluster within one year.
- Markets: no Wisconsin-specific contract found on Polymarket, Manifold, or via search of Kalshi; the only measles contracts are US-wide calendar-2026 CDC-counter thresholds, which differ from this question on geography, source, and threshold.

SERIES BASE RATES — reported statewide 2026 total by date (DHS, via DHS releases and contemporaneous coverage): Aug 25: 61 | Aug 28: 98 | Sep 1: 108-110 | Sep 4: 136-142 | Sep 8: 159 | Sep 11: 163 | Sep 15: 164 | Sep 16: 166 | Sep 18: 167.
Observed increments over windows the same length as the ~11-day remaining horizon, in this same series:
  - over the growth phase: Aug 28 -> Sep 8 = +61; Sep 1 -> Sep 11 = +53.
  - over the current phase: Sep 8 -> Sep 18 = +8 (0.8/day); Sep 11 -> Sep 18 (7 days) = +4; Sep 15 -> Sep 18 (3 days) = +3.
Conditional framing: the unconditional class 'US state measles outbreaks' has a very wide final-size distribution (Wisconsin's own 2025 = 36; 2026 Texas = 192, Utah = 527, PA = 767). The relevant conditioning variable is already known — this outbreak is ~6 weeks old and its weekly increment has fallen from ~+49 (week to Sep 8) to ~+5 (week to Sep 15). Conditional on that decline pattern, past outbreak tails add a low single-digit percent of cumulative over ~11 days; conditional on a NEW introduction into a separate low-vaccination community (which happened in this state in 2025 and produced 25 cases in weeks), the 11-day addition can be an order of magnitude larger.
Component rates to keep separate: (a) SW outbreak local transmission, currently ~+3 to +5/week and falling; (b) sporadic travel-associated introductions elsewhere in the state, which produced Marathon and Vernon cases within a single week against a national backdrop of 3,471 cases.
Measles mechanics: 10-21 day incubation, ~14-day generation interval, so cases posted between now and Oct 1 reflect infections from roughly Sep 4-17; one full generation, not two, fits inside the remaining horizon.

Weekly increments have decelerated monotonically and sharply: +46 (Aug 28-Sep 4), +19 (Sep 4-11), +4 (Sep 11-18). Of that last +4, three cases were outside the original outbreak (Marathon travel, two Vernon); the core Grant/Iowa/Lafayette confirmed count moved only 155->156 in a week, i.e. the primary outbreak has largely stalled as the susceptible pool depletes and MMR uptake rises. Prior from post-peak state-outbreak tails implies ~+4% over 12 days (~174); I shade the median slightly below that to 173 for the stall, and keep a fat right tail. Upside mechanisms: Vernon County has the state's lowest MMR coverage (42% of two-year-olds, >=1 dose) and two cases confirmed Sep 16 now folded into the outbreak, plus continued travel introductions amid 3,471 US cases in 47 states, plus occasional retrospective batch additions (a +49 week occurred in early September). But the 10-21 day incubation puts most Vernon secondary cases after Oct 1, which caps the pre-deadline upside. No market matching this contract exists on Polymarket, Manifold, or Kalshi (Polymarket's US-total-2026 measles event differs on geography, threshold and resolution source, so it is evidence not an anchor); p_above_upper of 1.5% prices a return to the late-August pace compressed into the pre-deadline window.

Dashboard updates twice weekly, so resolution likely reads a Sep 29-30 figure: ~11-12 days of accrual. Prior from the reference class of US state measles outbreaks ~6 weeks in and 2-3 weeks past their reporting peak (TX/NM 2025, UT/SC 2026): ~4-6% of cumulative added per 12 days, giving ~175. Non-trivial mass sits on 168-170 (including the case where the count barely moves or the last pre-deadline update is stale). Escape above 240 (+73 in 12 days) needs a full second exponential leg detected en masse or a definitional change: priced at 3%.

calls.reconciliation: Baseline (167 as of the Sep 18 DHS outbreaks page) was undisputed across all three dossiers, as was the absence of any DHS update after Sep 18 and the absence of any Wisconsin-specific prediction market. Four disputes: (1) update cadence - Run 1 said Tue/Fri, Run 2 Mon/Fri, Run 3 Sep 29-30; the shared observed posting dates (Sep 1, 4, 8, 11, 15, 18) fit early-week-plus-Friday, so the resolving post is ~Sep 28-Oct 1 and accrual is 10-12 days rather than the full 13. (2) Wastewater recency - Run 3's undated 'continued to be detected' loses to Run 1's dated claim (samples collected week of Aug 24, no other site positive) corroborated by Run 2's explicit null for September; I take the last confirmed detections as late August. (3) Vernon acquisition route - Run 3 calls one case locally acquired, Run 2 reports DHS declined to confirm linkage; this could NOT be settled from the dossiers and I let it carry its uncertainty, which matters less than it looks because 10-21 day incubation puts Vernon-seeded secondary cases largely past the Oct 1 read either way. (4) A minor arithmetic gap - two dossiers report 158 confirmed + 6 probable + 1 Marathon = 165 against a 167 headline; unresolvable here and irrelevant, since the headline total is the resolving instrument. The remaining disagreement is pure judgment - how much weight the Vernon introduction and continued travel seeding deserve against a core outbreak that added one confirmed case in a week. I took the decelerating-core reading, which lands my median at 174 and my p90 at 187, tighter on the right than Runs 2 and 3 because the incubation clock, not the susceptible pool, is what caps the pre-deadline upside. I carried forward Run 1's series and Run 3's conditional reference class, which I agree with; my dispersion is computed from this series' own tail-phase increment variability rather than the unconditional outbreak class.
